name: Condensed declaration
observed: Tall, narrow uppercase strokes make a compact, emphatic text mass. Tight line spacing and shared edges create the graphic; one contrasting ink and bare garment keep it legible. Distress appears in some examples, not all.
essential: The words must carry the situation. Preserve readable counters, deliberate line rhythm and a coherent text silhouette; emphasis must follow meaning.
flexible: Plain or weathered edges; one restrained accent; center or modest offset; moderate to large scale. A small icon can support already clear copy.
garment: Observed: crew-neck fronts in light and dark solids, fitted and relaxed silhouettes. A large block needs uninterrupted chest space; do not infer identical fit from identical mockups.
fit: A plausible fit for audiences who enjoy direct statements or verbal humor. Fails when the audience or situation exists only in an invisible illustration. CAR: WRONG needs more image evidence than a pure type version supplies.
failure: Too many independently enlarged words; illegible condensed counters; a tiny illustration asked to explain the whole premise.
detail: Compare repeated vertical strokes and compact leading. Here the setup and body form one text unit; source hierarchy is not automatically the right hierarchy for new copy.
metric: Anchor print width is about 62% of visible torso width at print level (0.39 / 0.63 image widths). The total print box is about 1.77 times wider than high. These are manual mockup estimates, not garment specifications.
proposal: Try at most one payoff accent. Select line breaks after assigning semantic roles, not by filling a rectangle.
status: provisional visual family / analyst interpretation; not purchase validated

name: Quiet vignette and dry caption
observed: One isolated figure or object sits in open garment space. A short, plain caption behaves like an aside. The graphic may be line drawing, naturalistic cutout or restrained cartoon; this is a deliberate subtype boundary, not proof those styles are interchangeable.
essential: A recognisable silhouette and a short verbal afterthought must work together at modest scale. Empty fabric is part of the composition.
flexible: Caption above or below; one ink or a subdued accent; centered placement or a purposeful offset. Figure style is a recorded subtype, chosen for the audience.
garment: Observed: mostly solid crew-neck fronts with ample blank torso. Folded Etsy images hide full scale; use whole-shirt references for placement decisions. Tiny left-chest marks are boundary examples, not the default.
fit: Useful for quiet, observant humor when a single object supplies the missing context. Less suitable for a sequence, multiple relationships or subtle antique details that disappear when reduced.
failure: Confusing restraint with undersizing; a fine drawing that turns into an indistinct spot; a caption so small that the payoff vanishes.
detail: The low, horizontal figure and nearby small caption share a single compact footprint. The open space around them does more work than decoration would.
metric: Anchor print width is about 53% of visible torso width at print level (0.32 / 0.60). Print aspect ratio is approximately 2.13:1. Small-looking does not mean a tiny measured print.
proposal: For a complex material, first simplify the visual relation; do not simply reduce the entire illustration.
status: provisional visual family / analyst interpretation; not purchase validated

name: Heritage illustrated emblem
observed: A detailed, recognisable hero sits between a curved or gently spread heading and a compact lower anchor. Serif or slab lettering, engraved or book-illustration marks, muted warm colors and open garment edges suggest a collected or timeworn object.
essential: Make the hero the context carrier; give lettering and illustration a shared vintage voice. Keep the outer silhouette open and distinguish headline, image and lower anchor without boxing every part.
flexible: Arch may flatten; color may be one ink plus an accent or a few muted fills; fine hatching may simplify. Naturalistic and friendly storybook subtypes must be kept distinct.
garment: Observed: pale, heathered and washed-looking solids; crew necks and varied fits. Proposed CAR application: relaxed charcoal crew, warm cream and faded rust. Vintage appearance is visual; actual fabric weight or aging is not inferred.
fit: Promising for some antique/vintage hunters because familiar object illustration and aged print can reinforce the subject. Transfer to food lovers needs evidence of their aesthetic fit; the same frame alone is insufficient.
failure: A generic badge with no material-specific action; tiny engraved details carrying the joke; ornamental stars and dates added without meaning.
detail: Heading, aircraft silhouette and lower date form a wide-to-narrow rhythm. The garment supplies the gaps; there is no enclosing panel.
metric: Anchor print width is about 63% of visible torso width at print level (0.39 / 0.62). Print aspect ratio is approximately 1.34:1. Heading occupies roughly the upper fifth of the print box; this is an estimate, not a fixed recipe.
proposal: For CAR: WRONG, replace the solitary hero with a clearly related antique cabinet and small open-boot car. Keep the setup at one weight and give the verdict a strong lower anchor.
status: provisional visual family / analyst interpretation; not purchase validated

name: Playful lettering and illustration interlock
observed: Broad rounded or irregular lettering shares its footprint with friendly outlined objects. Short copy and imagery nest into each other; two or three strong colors repeat across the unit. Open edges prevent the large composition from becoming a printed rectangle.
essential: Copy and image must feel drawn for each other while remaining readable. Match stroke weight and character; repeat palette roles. Give required semantic parts room before adding doodles.
flexible: A few rounded serif forms or hand-lettered capitals; light or dark base; two or three main inks; compact or broad silhouette. The illustration may interrupt a line without obscuring words.
garment: Observed: roomy and boxy fronts as well as regular crews; examples include ivory, dark navy and saturated color. Broad prints need breathing room inside the torso. Proposed charcoal application changes palette roles while retaining contrast.
fit: Promising for audiences who welcome approachable, cheerful humor and visible illustrations. Cute or bubbly treatment may weaken a solemn, austere or understated concept. Gendered store routes do not establish who will like it.
failure: Decorative clutter, many competing letter styles, equal emphasis everywhere, or cuteness that hides the actual transport problem.
detail: Coral letter masses and cobalt object outlines alternate in one vertical unit. Small secondary handwriting is subordinate; the cups are not a tiny icon beneath a finished headline.
metric: Anchor print width is about 75% of visible torso width at print level (0.55 / 0.73). Print aspect ratio is approximately 0.82:1. Main object band spans roughly one third of print height; pose and fabric folds make these coarse estimates.
proposal: For CAR: WRONG, fit two equally treated setup ideas into one line, then let the cabinet/car relationship occupy the middle and the punchline anchor the bottom. Omit unrelated flowers or stars.
status: provisional visual family / analyst interpretation; not purchase validated

name: Nostalgic display-letter wordmark
observed: Rounded, swollen or swashing display letters create the main image. Close spacing, nested words and warm or softened color pairings supply a nostalgic tone. The Bee & The Fox provides most core examples; other sources support only parts of this combination.
essential: Letterform personality and inter-word rhythm must carry the appeal. Preserve counters and joins while making the wordmark a coherent shape.
flexible: Bulbous sans, soft serif or ornamental swash are separate subtypes. Ringer trim can echo the ink, but is optional; warm contrast can shift to a cheerful high-contrast pairing.
garment: Observed: fitted ringer crews and regular/boxy tees. Trim color can complete the palette. A ringer-specific effect cannot be assumed to survive a plain POD blank unchanged.
fit: Useful when the wording itself is the desired identity signal and the audience welcomes nostalgic lettering. Evidence is concentrated in one brand; do not equate that brand audience with all women or antique hunters.
failure: Using an arbitrary retro font as the entire recipe; pinched letter counters; decorative swashes that interfere with the reading order.
detail: Cream lettering is compact and rounded; nearby collar/sleeve trim repeats the light color. The source is a styled, angled wearer photo, so garment-scale measurement is unreliable.
metric: Approximate artwork box aspect ratio: 1.69:1, using 0.33 of image width / 0.13 of image height on a 1000×1500 source. No torso-width ratio is reported because pose and partial occlusion distort it.
proposal: Test on short, self-contained copy first. A transport joke requiring a large picture is not the strongest initial transfer test.
status: provisional visual family / analyst interpretation; not purchase validated

name: Framed illustrated artifact
observed: An engraved, ornamental or storybook image lives inside a deliberate card-like boundary. A limited palette, integrated title/footer and fine internal pattern make a small illustrated artifact. Photographic panels and bright comic panels are retained as boundaries, not collapsed into this same visual voice.
essential: The boundary and interior must belong to one visual system. Maintain a dominant image, readable essential copy and a frame that survives shirt folds.
flexible: Rectangle, arch or ornamented perimeter; one or a few muted inks; modest or broad print. Texture may be clean or aged; line density must suit the reproduction size.
garment: Observed: solid fronts, including oversized and tucked styles. Tall panels occupy substantial torso height. This family can produce a valid tee, but lower text may disappear into a waistband or fold.
fit: Possible for audiences who enjoy collectible, gothic, bookish or decorative imagery. It is not automatically suitable for a quick visual joke or someone seeking a quiet everyday shirt.
failure: Defaulting to a poster page with many explanatory blocks; making essential narrative depend on tiny details; mistaking the existence of a border for style similarity.
detail: A thin double frame, patterned corners and integrated title anchor the engraved figure. The dark shirt is visible inside the illustration, reducing the sense of a solid pasted rectangle.
metric: Anchor print width is about 65% of visible torso width at print level (0.39 / 0.60). Print aspect ratio is approximately 0.64:1. The lower edge approaches the waist in this styled photo; actual printed dimensions are unknown.
proposal: Use only when the artifact-like presentation contributes to the identity or emotion. A border is not a cure for weak composition.
status: provisional visual family / analyst interpretation; not purchase validated

name: Faded outdoor color field
observed: A compact sun, horizon or landscape is reduced into layered shapes or a silhouette window. Cream, muted warm accents and cool/dark ground create a faded outdoor-patch feeling. Some examples add bold captions; the landscape still supplies the visual structure.
essential: Clear foreground/background separation and a readable silhouette; a deliberately limited color hierarchy; a bounded scene that remains a shirt-scale unit.
flexible: Round window, arched top or open skyline; two to several muted colors; little or substantial copy. Watercolor and neon variations remain boundaries, not interchangeable core recipes.
garment: Observed: dark regular crews and lighter casual blanks. The shirt can act as the deepest landscape layer. Changing the blank may require redrawing negative shapes, not merely switching ink color.
fit: Strong source context in outdoor interests, with transfers to nostalgia and sport. For unrelated audiences the sun/mountains may be irrelevant decoration; borrow shape relationships only if the new concept needs them.
failure: Adding a sunset to every subject; low contrast between successive layers; a background that competes with the required action.
detail: The pale circular field contains dark mountains and trees; one rust area provides depth. Outer edges are compact and the base cloth continues through the dark forms.
metric: Anchor print width is about 55% of visible torso width at print level (0.33 / 0.60). Print box is approximately square. Source image cannot establish ink count, physical texture or print technique.
proposal: For CAR: WRONG, a sunset does no essential semantic work. Keep this family available for a more suitable material instead of forcing it into the current test.
status: provisional visual family / analyst interpretation; not purchase validated

name: Airy handwritten signature
observed: Thin or moderately weighted cursive makes a personal-looking statement with plenty of blank fabric. A single flowing line or a loosely stacked short phrase remains the sole focus. Small left-chest embroidery is a process/placement boundary, not evidence that printed script will behave identically.
essential: A clear handwriting rhythm, legible joins and a quiet, single focal unit. Preserve visible contrast despite the relatively light strokes.
flexible: Single word or a short multi-line phrase; centered or left-chest position; one contrasting color. Scale must respond to word length and stroke thickness.
garment: Observed: light and dark casual crews, fitted/tucked and folded presentations. Folded mockups hide true torso and hem relationships. Do not rely on their styling accessories to make a plain blank desirable.
fit: Useful when a personal affiliation or emotionally direct phrase is self-explanatory. Weak initial choice for a situation requiring two objects, spatial comparison or a three-beat reveal.
failure: Hairline strokes disappearing in print; illegible joins; personal script mistaken for universal feminine taste; quietness used to justify an unclear concept.
detail: Connected low letters form a broad, shallow wordmark. Large surrounding blank space provides the restraint; the knot and styled props are not part of the artwork.
metric: Anchor print width is roughly 76% of visible torso width at print level (0.53 / 0.70), but folded edges make that denominator uncertain. Print aspect ratio is approximately 5.3:1. This is shallow, not necessarily physically small.
proposal: Test on a concise identity or emotional concept; do not force a cabinet/car drawing into the wordmark just to use the family.
status: provisional visual family / analyst interpretation; not purchase validated
